stem: A team's task always follows the same fixed steps: translate a document, check the translation against a glossary, then format it. They want predictable, consistent results. What should they build?

choices.text: A workflow: Claude and tools orchestrated through predefined code paths
choices.reason: Correct: workflows offer predictability and consistency for well-defined tasks like this one.

choices.text: An autonomous agent, because agents always perform better
choices.reason: Anthropic recommends the simplest solution possible; agents fit when flexibility and model-driven decisions are needed.

choices.text: An agent, because agents cost less and respond faster
choices.reason: The reverse: agentic systems often trade latency and cost for better task performance.

choices.text: A multi-agent system with one agent per step
choices.reason: More moving parts adds complexity without need; increase complexity only when simpler solutions fall short.

takeaway: Fixed, well-defined steps → **workflow**; open-ended problems needing model-driven decisions → **agent**.
mnemonic: Fixed path → workflow; open path → agent.

stem: Your coding agent usually finishes its task, but occasionally keeps calling tools without converging. Which safeguard does Anthropic's guidance recommend adding?

choices.text: Hide tool results from the agent so it can't get stuck on them
choices.reason: Agents need ground truth from the environment, such as tool results, at each step to assess progress.

choices.text: Trust the model to stop; agent tasks always terminate on completion
choices.reason: Tasks often end on completion, but the guidance adds stopping conditions precisely because that isn't guaranteed.

choices.text: Raise `max_tokens` so each turn can finish its thought
choices.reason: `max_tokens` caps a single response's length; it doesn't bound how many loop iterations run.

choices.text: A stopping condition such as a maximum number of iterations
choices.reason: Correct: it's common to include stopping conditions, such as a maximum number of iterations, to maintain control.

takeaway: Give every agent loop a **stopping condition** (e.g. an iteration cap), and feed it real tool results each step.
